title: The Gingerbread Man
summary: A freshly baked gingerbread man dashes away, meeting strangers who each try to catch him.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, within a secluded cottage overshadowed by ancient oaks, an old woman measured flour and molasses with trembling hands. She shaped the sweet dough into the distinct silhouette of a little man, pressing currants into the pale surface for eyes and buttons. Eager to see her creation take form, she carefully slid the baking tray into the roaring heat of the iron oven. The kitchen soon filled with the rich, spiced aroma of ginger and burnt sugar as the dough rose to a golden brown. Never did she imagine that the very confection she baked would possess a restless soul of its own.

When the brass door finally swung open, the little fellow did not wait for the residual heat to cool. With a sudden, astonishing burst of agility, he vaulted across the tiled floor and scrambled toward the open threshold. The old woman stood frozen in utter disbelief, her hands pressed against her apron as the runaway vanished into the morning sun. Panic seizing her breath, she raised her voice in a sharp, urgent cry demanding that he halt his frantic flight. Yet her desperate warnings dissolved harmlessly into the morning air, leaving her stranded in the doorway.

The fast runner simply laughed, a high, metallic sound that echoed mockingly against the stone walls of the cottage. He shouted back that he had escaped the blazing oven and would never return to the confines of a kitchen. Racing past the vegetable patch, he spotted an old man bent over the soil, weeding the damp earth with a rusted trowel. With reckless abandon, the gingerbread man called out that he possessed a speed far superior to any mortal pursuer. The gardener straightened up in astonishment, lunging forward with outstretched arms, but the nimble confection had already darted beyond his reach.

Further down the dusty country lane, the proud little traveler encountered a heavy farm animal laboring near a wooden fence. The beast paused, its large eyes locking onto the sprinting figure with immediate, predatory interest. Sensing a delectable treat, the animal lowered its head and lunged forward to intercept the runaway. Instead of yielding, the gingerbread man laughed louder still, taunting his new pursuer with the tale of his previous escapes. He boasted that he had outrun both the old woman and the gardener, and that no beast of burden could ever claim him. With every pounding stride across the turf, his confidence swelled into absolute arrogance.

Across emerald meadows and through the dappled shadows of a whispering pine forest, he maintained his relentless pace. To celebrate his glorious freedom, he composed a cheerful little song about his marvelous evasion, chanting it aloud to the empty woods. Not a single creature in the valley could match his velocity, for his legs felt as swift and untamable as the autumn wind. Yet every journey must eventually confront an obstacle, and soon the proud runner found his path obstructed by a broad, sluggish river. The water rushed deep and dark between steep banks, forcing the arrogant fugitive to skid to an abrupt halt.

Sitting quietly by the muddy edge was a cunning animal with sleek fur and an observant, calculating gaze. Recognizing the predicament of the breathless runner, the creature offered a smooth and seemingly generous solution to his dilemma. Because the gingerbread man possessed no means of crossing the treacherous current, he foolishly chose to place his trust in the stranger. Without a moment of hesitation, he leaped forward and perched lightly upon the tip of the animal's twitching tail. As they pushed off from the bank and drifted into the swirling water, the animal calmly suggested that the weight might be too much for the tail alone.

Midway across the channel, the current grew visibly stronger, churning into white foam against unseen rocks beneath the surface. True to its calculated strategy, the animal turned its head slightly and advised the traveler to climb higher for safety. The gingerbread man obediently scrambled up the wet spine, settling comfortably between the shoulder blades as the cold spray splashed around them. Yet the water continued to rise, lapping dangerously close to the passenger's delicate sugar crust. With an urgent tone of false concern, the cunning beast insisted that the little man must move yet again to avoid ruin.

Finally, as they drew agonizingly close to the opposite bank, the animal suggested that the traveler sit directly upon its snout. Only there, the creature argued, would the fragile confection remain completely dry until they stepped ashore. Blinded by his own supreme vanity and desperate to preserve his perfect form, the gingerbread man readily complied. The very second his sugary feet touched the tip of the nose, the clever animal tilted its head back with chilling precision. It opened its wide jaws and snapped them shut, ending the existence of the little fellow who believed he was far too clever for the world.

News of the astonishing spectacle spread through the surrounding countryside before the sun had even reached its zenith. The old woman received the reports with a heavy heart, mourning the loss of her extraordinary creation with profound grief. She wondered aloud if she would ever possess the inspiration to bake such a wondrous thing again, though deep down she knew the magic was gone. The reckless journey of the little man transformed rapidly from a bizarre morning event into a legendary tale told across the entire province. Children playing near the overgrown garden would pause their games to ask their parents about the legendary runner.

Every resident in the neighboring village knew the narrative by heart, repeating the sequence of events with grim fascination. They maintained a steadfast belief that no living creature could ever rival the raw speed of the gingerbread man. Yet the river continued its timeless descent, flowing silently past the green pastures where the dramatic pursuit had originally unfolded. Along those very banks, local wildlife frequently lingered, watching travelers with a quiet, calculating intensity. Those creatures were rarely as benevolent as their outward demeanor might initially suggest to an unsuspecting observer.

True wisdom, the elders whispered to the rising generation, required far more than mere athletic prowess or blinding speed. Trust should never be granted lightly, especially to strangers offering unsolicited assistance in times of sudden peril. The tragic fate of the little runner served as a permanent reminder that arrogance often blinds us to imminent danger. Even today, parents across the valley recount the cautionary tale to ensure their children remember the hidden perils of the world. Thus, the legacy of the spiced traveler endured, etched forever into the memory of the river valley.
